subject: MSA / Order Form — claim notice lifecycle and escrow handoff proposal
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@novushealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 12 Mar 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: MSA / Order Form — proposed approach to notice window & escrow handoff

Hi Sara — great to be moving forward. Quick legal question that came up in our internal redline pass: Novus asked for a 120‑day extended notice window for third‑party IP claims and a requirement that we maintain an escrow-ready evidence bundle for 24 months. Legal (cc'd) flagged two operational risks here: the operational burden of evidence custodian + potential dispute over when escrow is triggered.

Proposal from our side to keep momentum:
- Keep the customer notice window at 60 days (we can agree to use commercially reasonable efforts to surface claims earlier).
- For evidence/escrow: accept a "reasonable evidence preservation" obligation and an explicit trigger for escrow (e.g., final determination or settlement call) rather than automatic escrow on notice.
- Add an SLA for evidence handoff timeline (30 business days from trigger) and a documented handoff contact.

Attaching our redlines and an ops diagram for the evidence handoff. Can we get Novus legal's comfort on the escrow trigger language? If they need escrow automatic on notice, we will need to scope additional costs in the order form.

Next steps: if legal is comfortable with the trigger-and-SLA approach, we can fold into the order form and close the procurement PO.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: [Novus_MSA_redlines_20250312.pdf]

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@novushealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Novus Health Legal <legal@novushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Mar 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — proposed approach to notice window & escrow handoff

Ben — thanks for the quick note and the redlines. Two internal asks from procurement/legal: 1) We need a 120‑day notice window to align with our internal claim triage workflows (clinical/legal ops). 2) Automatic escrow on notice is our standard for any third‑party IP claims tied to clinical safety.

That said, we understand the operational lift. Please have your legal propose explicit acceptance criteria for the evidence bundle (what metadata, logs, samples are required) and a named person/team responsible for evidence export. If we can operationalize the exchange, we may be able to accept a staged escrow where the data is preserved but access requires mutually agreed trigger events.

Can Kimberly and Marissa review and propose concrete wording?

—Sara
Sara Liu | Sr. Procurement Manager, Novus Health

From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@novushealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 13 Mar 2025 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — proposed approach to notice window & escrow handoff

Sara / Ben — thanks, context is helpful. Draft position below (high level) we can convert to redline language: 

1) Notice window: Redwood agrees to use commercially reasonable efforts to notify Novus promptly and, absent extraordinary circumstances, within 60 days of becoming aware. If Novus requires 120 days as a condition of procurement, we can accept 120 days but request a mutual cooperation clause (mutual remediation timeline and escalation path) to avoid unilateral stale claims.

2) Evidence preservation and escrow: Redwood will preserve relevant evidence (logs, model artifacts, request/response samples, and custody metadata) for 24 months. Automatic physical escrow (duplication and transfer of artifacts to a third‑party escrow agent) will be required only upon (a) written agreement to settle or (b) a final adjudication that requires such transfer. Until that trigger, Redwood will maintain the preserved package and provide secure access for Novus legal and their appointed forensic vendor under a joint non‑disclosure and access protocol.

3) SLA and handoff: Upon trigger, Redwood will provide an evidence handoff within 30 business days. If escrow transfer is required, Redwood will initiate transfer within 10 business days after the handoff acceptance. Redwood proposes a $X,XXX fee (to be added to the order form) if Novus insists on automatic escrow at notice to cover duplication, storage, and third‑party escrow agent fees.

I have attached suggested redline snippets that translate the above into MSA + Order Form language (see attachment). High‑level ask for Novus legal: confirm whether the staged-access-with-trigger is acceptable, or confirm they need automatic escrow on notice (we will then issue a cost addendum).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
attachments: [Novus_MSA_redlines_20250312.pdf, evidence-handback-process-diagram.png]

From: Novus Health Legal <legal@novushealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@novushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2025 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — proposed approach to notice window & escrow handoff

Kimberly — thank you for the clear proposal and the redlines. We are generally comfortable with the staged preservation + access model but Novus legal needs two clarifications before we can accept non‑automatic escrow: 

1) Evidence acceptance criteria: please provide a concise checklist (we need to ensure forensic reproducibility: time‑stamped request/response, model version/weights hash, and an explanation of any redaction applied).
2) Access protocol: we need a written process for how Novus engages a third‑party forensic vendor, including expected response times, authentication, and egress controls.

If Redwood can provide those two items as a supplement to the MSA and confirm the 30 business day handoff, Novus is willing to accept escrow-on-trigger language. If not, we will revert to our standard automatic escrow on notice and ask procurement to include the escrow service fees in the PO.

Please confirm by EOD Wednesday so procurement can finalize the SOW and PO.

—Novus Health Legal

From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Novus Health Legal <legal@novushealth.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@novushealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 18 Mar 2025 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — proposed approach to notice window & escrow handoff

Thanks — noted. We will: 
- Produce a 1‑page evidence acceptance checklist (hashes, timestamps, sample counts, redaction flags) by tomorrow morning.
- Draft an access protocol (roles, auth, timeline) for Novus review by EOD Thursday.
- Confirm the 30 business day handoff and outline a cost schedule if Novus requires automatic escrow on notice.

Marissa / Mateo — can you own the checklist + access protocol drafts? Ben, I will include the estimated escrow cost line for procurement.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
